This bechina pair is not captured in the dataset. The concept of 'setting God before oneself' is a distinct thematic domain from the main יד הגדולה/הסתפקות package — it appears as an appended teaching at the end of the Torah (line 6) and its thematic connection to the main teaching is not elaborated. It does not belong cleanly to Package 1 (which is about divine provision/contentment via maaser). It may belong to a separate, underdeveloped cluster, or may be a fragment pointing to a cross-reference.

analysis_notes.note_on_eitza_edges: All other reference=221 edges in the dataset are type 'eitza', not 'bechina'. They record causal flows: maaser → contentment (id=920), maaser → Great Hand (id=1245, 1246), contentment → God extends His hand and saves from enemies (id=978), Great Hand → God extends His hand and saves from enemies (id=979), giving maaser → saved from enemies (id=2179). These are correctly classified as eitza and do not generate package membership.
analysis_notes.torah_structure_note: Torah #221 is a short, tightly-argued teaching. Its argument: (1) giving maaser saves from enemies because God covers/protects the person with His hand; (2) this protective covering is possible because the Great Hand = contentment/sufficiency; (3) maaser produces the state of contentment; (4) therefore through maaser God extends His Great Hand and protects. The single bechina equation (יד הגדולה = הסתפקות) is the conceptual pivot of the entire Torah. The appended line about שִׁוִּיתִי/מִתְנַגֵּד appears to be a separate, underdeveloped observation that is not integrated into the main argument.
